title: The Science Behind Coffee, Caffeine, and Stress
summary: Have you ever wondered why you feel stressed every time you drink cofffee? A deeper understanding of caffeine’s role in elevating stress is essential, especially if you work at a high stress job, are prone to caffeine’s anxiety inducing effects, or are just seeking a calmer lifestyle. Moreover, there is an emerging alternative to regular coffee, called Px coffee, that offers the alertness of caffeine without ramping up your body’s stress response.
body_text: The Science of Caffeine & Stress For many of us, coffee is an essential morning (and often afternoon) ritual. The aroma, the warmth, and the energizing jolt it provides can transform a groggy start into a productive day. Yet, there’s a hidden side to your daily brew that few of us like to talk about: how regular coffee can contribute to and exacerbate stress, anxiety, and burnout if consumed in excess or at the wrong times. While coffee itself has various health benefits, such as antioxidants and potential cognitive perks, its primary active ingredient, caffeine, isn’t always the benign pick-me-up we believe it to be. In recent years, a growing body of research points to caffeine’s adverse effects on the body’s stress response. It’s not all doom and gloom - moderate coffee consumption can be part of a balanced lifestyle for many people - but many of us are overconsuming caffeine and relying on it as a crutch to help push through workplace burnout and exhaustion. In short, a deeper understanding of caffeine’s role in elevating stress is essential, especially if you work at a high stress job, are prone to caffeine’s anxiety inducing effects, or are just seeking a calmer lifestyle. Moreover, there is an emerging alternative to regular coffee, called Px coffee, that offers the alertness of caffeine without ramping up your body’s stress response. In this blog post, we’ll explore five science-backed reasons why your regular coffee habit may be amplifying and elevating your stress levels. We’ll also share more about why Px coffee could be a simple solution to help reduce your day-to-day stress. 1. Caffeine spikes cortisol Cortisol — often referred to as the “stress hormone”— is a key player in the body’s fight-or-flight response. While cortisol is essential for various bodily functions (including metabolism and immune responses), chronically elevated levels are associated with a range of issues, from impaired cognition to weight gain and even cardiovascular strain. The Cortisol-Caffeine Link: Immediate Boost in Cortisol: When you drink coffee, the caffeine binds to adenosine receptors in your brain, reducing the sensation of tiredness. Large amounts of caffeine also trigger your body to release adrenaline and cortisol, shocking your nervous system into a state of high alertness. For example, most studies point to a measurable spike in cortisol levels within 30 to 60 minutes of caffeine consumption ( Lovallo, 2005) . Stress Response Amplification: This hormonal spike doesn’t just make you alert; it can also leave you feeling wired or on edge, particularly if you already have a baseline level of stress. You can read more about this effect in our cortisol blog post . Caffeine & Cortisol: Why it matters While an occasional boost in cortisol isn’t harmful—after all, the fight-or-flight response evolved to help us survive immediate threats—modern life often demands continuous mental performance. If you’re drinking multiple cups of coffee throughout the day, you may be chronically stimulating cortisol release. Over time, chronic cortisol elevation is correlated with disrupted sleep patterns, lowered immune function, and a persistent feeling of stress or anxiety. In the long term, it can lead to feelings of burnout at work if you are consistently in a state of heightened alertness ( read more about coffee and burnout here ). Key Takeaway #1 Pay attention to both the timing and quantity of your coffee. Consuming coffee right after you wake up, or sipping multiple cups in quick succession, can create a stress hormone roller coaster. Monitoring how your body responds—particularly if you notice increased stress or irritability—can help you adjust your habits. For those who find caffeine especially taxing, exploring alternatives such as Px coffee – more on this below – may offer a smoother, less stress-inducing energy boost. 2. Caffeine overstimulates and causes anxiety-like symptoms Another core reason why your regular coffee might be elevating your stress is tied to the overstimulation of your nervous system. Again, caffeine directly impacts your central nervous system by blocking adenosine (a naturally occurring neuromodulator that promotes relaxation and sleep). While blocking adenosine keeps you from feeling drowsy, it also ramps up neurotransmitters like dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine, which are all related to heightened alertness and, in some cases, anxiety or panic attacks. How caffeine overstimulation occurs Blocking Adenosine Receptors: Adenosine’s job is to calm the nervous system. When caffeine hijacks those receptors, your body doesn’t receive signals to slow down, leading to heightened electrical activity in the brain. Increased Heart Rate and Blood Pressure: Along with mental alertness, you may experience a racing heart or elevated blood pressure. This physiological stress response can feel identical to anxiety or even mild panic, especially if you’re already predisposed to anxious feelings. Fight-or-Flight Trigger: When your sympathetic nervous system is constantly in a “go” mode, minor inconveniences can feel overwhelming. This perception of stress can start a vicious cycle: You feel stressed -> You drink coffee to “wake up” and handle it -> You become more stressed from the coffee -> You drink more coffee. Research on caffeine-induced anxiety A 2024 study ( Liu, 2024 ) found that people who consumed high amounts of caffeine (generally above four cups of standard coffee) had a highly significant increase in the risk of anxiety. Participants who consume more caffeine daily report more instances of nervousness, increased heart rate, and difficulty concentrating. For those with pre-existing anxiety disorders, large amounts of caffeine can intensify symptoms and lead to heightened stress ( Klevebrandt, 2022 ). Key Takeaway #2 If you notice jitteriness, an overactive mind, or your stress levels rising after a few cups of coffee, you might be pushing your nervous system too far. Consider scaling back or switching to a milder form of stimulation. Caffeine amplifies existing feelings of stress and anxiety. 3. The Caffeine Crash Cycle It’s not just the immediate jolt of stress you feel after a cup of coffee; it’s the often inevitable “crash” that follows once that initial burst of caffeine wears off. The caffeine crash cycle can contribute to emotional and physiological fatigue, as your body swings from a stimulated state to a sudden energy drop. Why does the caffeine crash happen? The caffeine crash isn’t just about the caffeine wearing off — it’s a combination of biochemical processes that leave you feeling exhausted and mentally foggy. Here’s what happens: Adenosine Rebound Effect: Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors in the brain, preventing feelings of drowsiness. However, adenosine continues to accumulate in the background while caffeine is active, essentially building up in amount. As caffeine is metabolized and leaves the system, adenosine floods back into its receptors all at once, leading to a sudden wave of fatigue and sluggishness ( i.e., the caffeine crash). Stress Response Wear-Off: As described above, caffeine activates the stress response by increasing cortisol and adrenaline levels. Once the stimulant fades, the body experiences a rebound effect, where stress hormones subside, leaving you feeling more drained. This can exacerbate feelings of burnout and make it difficult to stay productive. Key Takeaway #3 The caffeine crash isn’t just about low energy—it’s the result of a rapid neurochemical shift, where adenosine floods back in and stress hormones drop. This leaves many people feeling exhausted, anxious, or in need of another cup of coffee—perpetuating the cycle. 4. Genetic Variations & Sensitivity One significant yet often overlooked factor that influences how coffee affects stress levels is genetic variation. Not everyone metabolizes caffeine the same way. Genetics can dictate your caffeine “speed limit,” determining how quickly or slowly you break down and clear caffeine from your system. Additionally, genetic differences in the adenosine receptors in the brain (the ones caffeine interacts with) are associated with increased risk of caffeine-induced anxiety. This genetic lottery can mean the difference between feeling cool, calm, and collected after a latte or feeling shaky and anxious. Key genetic factors influcence caffeine sensitivity CYP1A2 Gene: This gene encodes an enzyme that helps metabolize caffeine in the liver. Some individuals carry a variant that works quickly, while others have a slower version. Slow metabolizers experience caffeine’s effects (and side effects) more intensely and for a longer duration. ADORA2 Gene: Variations in the ADORA2 gene, which encode the adenosine receptors, can make you more susceptible to caffeine-induced anxiety attacks ( Alsene, 2003 ; Childs, 2008) . Personalized stress risks of caffeine sensitization Slow Metabolizers: If you’re a slow metabolizer, a single cup of coffee might cause lingering stimulation that leads to an elevated baseline of stress throughout the day. Heightened Anxiety Response: For those with ADORA2A variants, even moderate caffeine intake can lead to increased stress responses and caffeine-induced anxiety. Key Takeaway #4 Genetic testing or paying close attention to your reactions can help you discover whether you’re particularly sensitive to caffeine’s stress- and anxiety-inducing effects.If you find that standard coffee leaves you jittery or anxious, you may want to explore specialized alternatives like Px coffee. In addition to being metabolized faster than caffeine, it interacts with the adenosine receptors differently (see Okuro, 2010) and may help reduce or eliminate some of the stress-related symptoms associated with caffeine sensitivity. Your genetics affects how you process and experience caffeine. 5. Sleep Disruption and The Vicious Cycle of Stress We’ve all been there: You rely on coffee to power through a busy day, only to find yourself tossing and turning at night. Poor sleep then sets the stage for increased stress the following day, which—ironically—makes you crave even more coffee. This creates a vicious cycle of perpetual stress and fatigue. Caffeine’s Effect on Sleep Delayed Melatonin Release: Caffeine can interfere with your body’s production of melatonin, the hormone responsible for regulating sleep cycles ( Shilo, 2002 ). Decreased Slow-Wave Sleep: Caffeine, even when consumed 6 or more hours before going to bed, affects sleep quality ( Drake, 2013 ). This stage of sleep is crucial for physical restoration and stress hormone regulation. Next-Day Stress: When you lack adequate restorative sleep, your body experiences elevated cortisol levels the next morning. You may feel more anxious or irritable, which then drives you back to coffee for relief—creating a cycle that can be tough to break. Stressful Consequences Lack of quality sleep not only makes you physically tired but also heightens emotional reactivity. Small problems can seem like big ones, and you may find your capacity to handle daily stressors is greatly diminished. Over time, chronic sleep debt can exacerbate symptoms of anxiety and stress-related disorders. Key Takeaway #5 If your daily coffee habit is encroaching on your sleep, try limiting caffeine to just the mornings, or reducing the amount of caffeine you consume in the afternoon. Px Coffee: A Low-Stress Alternative By now, we’ve established multiple ways in which regular caffeinated coffee can lead to increased stress, from cortisol spikes to overstimulation, crashes, genetic sensitivities, and sleep disruption. If these issues resonate with you, there’s good news: You don’t have to give up your beloved coffee ritual. Px coffee, a coffee option made with paraxanthine instead of standard caffeine, is emerging as a modern solution for coffee drinkers who are feeling stressed out, overworked, and burned out. What Is Paraxanthine (Px)? Paraxanthine, or Px, is a primary metabolite of caffeine. In other words, when you drink coffee, your body converts some of the caffeine into paraxanthine over time. Several studies point to paraxanthine offering the cognitive benefits of caffeine (such as increased alertness and focus) but with fewer downsides related to stress and anxiety. Why Paraxanthine Over Caffeine? Smoother Energy Curve: Anecdotal reports and preliminary research indicate paraxanthine may produce a steadier boost in alertness without the intense peaks and valleys. This is likely because paraxanthine crosses the blood-brain barrier slower than caffeine and it binds tighter to adenosine receptors. Lower Anxiety Response: A rodent study found that paraxanthine had less of an effect on anxiety as compared to caffeine ( Okura, 2010); another study reported that paraxanthine, at low doses, spiked stress hormones less than caffeine ( Benowitz, 1995 ). Fewer Sleep Disturbances: Because paraxanthine is metabolized faster than caffeine ( Birkett, 1986 ), many Px coffee users report sleeping better. In fact, about 55% of people who switched to Px coffee self-report sleeping better at night. How Px Coffee works Px coffee is coffee. The only difference is the caffeine has been swapped out and replaced with Px, giving it a more refined profile of stimulatory effects: Support for Stress Management: If cortisol control and stress reduction are personal health goals, Px coffee might help you achieve a balance. Rather than contributing to stress, it’s designed to minimize your body’s stress response. Preventing and coping with burnout: Px coffee aims to deliver the energy and focus you need to power through long workdays, but without triggering the roller coaster of nervous system overstimulation and fatigue found with standard coffee. Is Px Coffee Right for You? If you’ve noticed any of the following, Px coffee may be a worthwhile consideration: You feel burned out and you use regular coffee to push through the day. You struggle with afternoon energy slumps or a “caffeine crash.” You have difficulty winding down at night and believe caffeine may be interfering with your sleep. You’re curious about cutting-edge coffee innovations that fit a healthier, less stress-prone lifestyle. Enjoy your coffee without extra stress In our fast-paced world, coffee often feels like a non-negotiable staple. However, as we’ve seen through these five reasons, traditional caffeine consumption can elevate stress levels by spiking cortisol, overstimulating the nervous system, causing energy crashes, interacting with genetic predispositions, and disrupting sleep. If you recognize any of these stress triggers in your own coffee habit, it might be time to reevaluate how and what you’re drinking. Px coffee offers a novel approach by focusing on paraxanthine, a metabolite of caffeine meant to deliver the energy and focus we crave without caffeine’s stress-amplifying side effects. Ultimately, understanding your own body’s response to caffeine is the first step in managing stress effectively. Paying attention to your energy levels, mood, and sleep quality after each cup can guide you in making healthier choices. Whether that means cutting back on traditional coffee or switching over to a paraxanthine-based alternative, the goal is clear: enjoy your coffee ritual without sacrificing mental well-being.

title: Mudrex Crypto Market Recap | Feb 18, 2025 – Feb 24, 2025
summary: This week proved that the crypto market is becoming increasingly resilient to shocks. Despite experiencing the largest crypto hack in history, the market held steady thanks to swift crisis management and clear communication. Meanwhile, major players like Google and the U.S. Federal Reserve made significant moves that could shape Bitcoin’s future and global liquidity trends. […]
body_text: This week proved that the crypto market is becoming increasingly resilient to shocks. Despite experiencing the largest crypto hack in history, the market held steady thanks to swift crisis management and clear communication. Meanwhile, major players like Google and the U.S. Federal Reserve made significant moves that could shape Bitcoin’s future and global liquidity trends. Let’s dive into the biggest developments in crypto this week and what they mean for the market. The Largest Crypto Hack Ever: Bybit Loses $1.5 Billion Bybit, the second-largest exchange by trading volume, suffered a massive security breach, losing nearly $1.5 billion in digital assets. The hacker gained unauthorized access to one of the exchange’s cold wallets and drained large amounts of mETH (Mantle Staked Ethereum) and stETH (Lido Staked Ethereum) before swapping them for ETH on decentralized exchanges. To put this into perspective, crypto-related thefts in 2025 have already reached 70% of 2024’s total $2.2 billion losses, and it’s only February. This underscores the persistent security challenges facing the industry. Bybit’s CEO, Ben Zhou, quickly addressed the situation, reassuring users that the exchange remains solvent and that all other cold wallets are secure. Additionally, Bybit coordinated with other major exchanges to blacklist the hacker’s wallet addresses, limiting the attacker’s ability to liquidate the stolen funds. What’s remarkable is that the crypto market remained stable despite this massive hack. Normally, such an event could trigger panic selling, but Bybit’s quick response helped prevent FUD (Fear, Uncertainty, and Doubt) from spreading. This reflects the industry’s growing maturity and ability to handle crises effectively. Google Exploring Bitcoin Wallet Logins: A Game Changer or a Privacy Risk? A Web3 specialist recently revealed that Google is working on integrating its authentication services with Bitcoin wallets, aiming to simplify user access to digital assets. The move is part of a broader effort by Google to improve blockchain usability and lower entry barriers for mainstream adoption. While this initiative could make Bitcoin more accessible to everyday users, it has sparked debate within the crypto community: Potential Benefits: Easier Access – Users could log into Bitcoin wallets with Google credentials, making it more user-friendly. Mainstream Adoption – A major tech giant embracing Bitcoin could accelerate its global adoption. Enhanced Security – Google’s infrastructure could help reduce phishing attacks and unauthorized access. Concerns and Risks: Privacy Issues – Storing Bitcoin wallet access credentials with a centralized entity contradicts the decentralized ethos of crypto. Security Risks – If Google’s authentication system is compromised, linked Bitcoin wallets could be at risk. Regulatory Scrutiny – Governments may push for more oversight, reducing Bitcoin’s permissionless nature. Adding to the security discussion, Google is also researching Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP) to improve privacy and encryption between on-chain and off-chain systems. If implemented correctly, ZKPs could enhance security while maintaining the ease of access that Google aims to provide. The Fed May Pause Quantitative Tightening (QT) Soon—A Boost for Crypto? The Federal Reserve is approaching its goal of keeping around $3 trillion in bank reserves, which means it may soon pause its balance sheet reduction process—known as Quantitative Tightening (QT). Why Does This Matter for Crypto? The U.S. Treasury needs to issue a large number of short-term Treasury bonds (T-bills) to rebuild cash reserves. However, there’s no extra liquidity cushion in the financial system, making it harder for banks to absorb these bonds. The Fed is closely monitoring the risk of a cash shortage, similar to the 2019 repo market crisis. If the Fed slows or stops QT, it would mean more liquidity in the financial system, which could benefit risk assets like Bitcoin and crypto. Historically, more liquidity leads to higher asset prices, and Bitcoin has often thrived in loose monetary conditions. However, short-term volatility could still occur if Treasury bond issuance drains liquidity faster than expected. European Central Bank (ECB) Adopting Blockchain for Payments The European Central Bank (ECB) has announced plans to integrate Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) into its payment infrastructure. This move could pave the way for a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) and revolutionize cross-border transactions. How Will It Work? Phase 1: The ECB will integrate blockchain technology into the TARGET payment system, its existing settlement infrastructure. Phase 2: A more advanced blockchain-based system will be explored for long-term adoption. Why Is This Important? Faster Transactions: Blockchain can reduce settlement times from days to seconds. Enhanced Security: DLT can lower fraud and hacking risks by improving transaction transparency. Less Dependence on U.S. Payment Systems: The ECB wants to reduce reliance on non-European payment providers and strengthen the eurozone economy. The ECB is expected to release more details soon, but this move signals that even traditional financial institutions see blockchain as the future of payments. What’s Next? While the Bybit hack was a major blow, the quick response from the exchange and the broader industry highlights crypto’s increasing resilience. Looking ahead, investors should keep an eye on another major event: Solana (SOL) Token Unlock – Will It Impact Prices? On March 1, around 11.2 million SOL tokens (worth over $2 billion) will be unlocked as part of FTX’s bankruptcy process. Since these tokens were previously locked, their sudden release into the market could have significant effects on SOL’s price and liquidity. If large amounts of SOL are sold immediately, it could lead to downward pressure on the price. If investors absorb the supply without panic selling, SOL’s price could remain stable or even recover. Some traders may view this as a buying opportunity if prices dip temporarily. The coming days will reveal whether Solana holders will face turbulence or whether the market will absorb the unlock smoothly. Either way, traders should be prepared for potential volatility. Final Thoughts This week showcased both the challenges and resilience of the crypto market. The Bybit hack was a major setback, but the market’s stability in its aftermath signals growing maturity. Meanwhile, Google’s Bitcoin wallet integration, the Fed’s monetary policy shifts, and the ECB’s blockchain adoption indicate that crypto is becoming more deeply embedded into global finance. As always, staying informed and prepared is key in this fast-moving space.

title: Impact of Counterfeit Medications on Patient Care
summary: By Nurse Oluseun Ofuani-Geo
body_text: Impact of Counterfeit Medications on Patient Care Remedial Health 3 min read · Feb 18, 2025 -- By Nurse Oluseun Ofuani-George Press enter or click to view image in full size When Mrs O bought a “teething mixture” at a shop close to her house, she didn’t bargain that it would result in her baby needing surgery to correct the damage done. Baby O survived but it was a pretty close call as the acid mixture had caused some perforations in her digestive tract. Yes. The mixture was fake and I bet the pharmacy procurement team presumed they got it from a reliable source. This is only one case out of many that have happened as a result of ingesting counterfeit medications. What are Counterfeit Medications? Counterfeit medications are broadly defined as drugs that contains inadequate amounts of active ingredients, contain the wrong active ingredients, be contaminated with harmful substances, and/or be falsely labelled. Scary Statistics of Counterfeit Medicine In the last few months, illegal operations across the country have been freely circulating fake and substandard drugs as well as unwholesome food and drinks. This fraudulent practice, is putting the lives of many Nigerians on the line. In August 6, 2024, the NAFDAC informed healthcare providers and the public of a report confirming the presence of counterfeited Perjeta in Nigeria. Also, on November 21, 2024, NAFDAC announced the circulation of counterfeit Combiart Dispersible Tablet 20/120mg in the country. In December 18, 2024, NAFDAC alerted the public to the sale and distribution of counterfeit Paludex tablets and suspensions across Nigeria. NAFDAC reports that approximately 17 per cent of pharmaceutical products in circulation are counterfeit, putting millions of lives at risk. To put it more succinctly, the World Health Organization estimates that 1 in 10 medicines in low- and middle-income countries failed quality control tests, suggesting the product is substandard or falsified. That’s how serious this issue is. As a matter of fact, Hospitals are overwhelmed with cases of poisoning and organ failure as direct effects of ingesting these counterfeit medications. Negative Impact of Counterfeit Medications You may begin to wonder, how badly is this affecting us or what is the impact? Let me tell you: 1,It causes toxicity 2,Treatment failure 3,Exacerbation of diseases 4,Accelerating the spread of drug resistance 5,Making treatable diseases deadly 6,Financially, it depletes savings by making treatment more expensive as the intervention to correct the effects of counterfeit medication is not cheap. The picture is getting clearer, right? How to Combat Counterfeit Medications Solutions Insights into solving the problem? Okay, let’s go: 1, The use of technology in combating the issue. Provide modern technology for detecting counterfeit products, and expand enforcement powers. 2, Verification system using QR codes could allow consumers to verify the authenticity of products. 3, Anti-counterfeiting measures such as holographic labels and track-and-trace systems 4,Sensitization: Consumers needs to be aware of the risks associated with counterfeit goods and how to identify them. These measures would to a large extent curb this menace. What We Are Doing In Remedial Health? Remedial Health was birthed to directly combat this menace of counterfeit medication. As a pharmaceutical supply chain company, we specialise in bringing into the market, trusted and genuine medication. Do we offer the solutions listed above? YES and more. Our top notch pharmacy procurement team go straight to the source for procurement, leaving no room for middle men meddling as the case may be. So who’s your go to pharmaceutical supply chain brand? title: Vulnerability Report at ToDesktop on October 2nd, 2024
summary: A security researcher reported that they was able to gain access to leaked access tokens of ToDesktop’s Firebase Service Account. **We have reviewed logs and inspected app bundles. No malicious usage was detected. There were no malicious builds or releases of applications from the ToDesktop platform.**
body_text: Impact No customer data or applications were compromised Action required No action required from customers Resolution time 26 hours Summary On October 2nd 2024, a security researcher (T/A xyz3va) reported that she was able to gain access to ToDesktop’s Firebase Service Admin Account. We have reviewed logs and inspected app bundles. No malicious usage was detected. There were no malicious builds or releases of applications from the ToDesktop platform. We promptly patched the vulnerability and rotated all keys. In addition to patching the vulnerability, we engaged a third-party cybersecurity company, Doyensec , to conduct an independent audit of our platform and build pipeline. Timeline All timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Date and Time What Happened October 2nd, 6:36pm–6:58pm The researcher reported the vulnerability, and we acknowledged and confirmed it. October 2nd, 9:00pm Rotated all affected credentials. October 2nd, 10:00pm Conducted a preliminary review of logs and investigated recent releases, with no immediate signs of unauthorized access. October 3rd, 8:13pm Deployed a patch for the vulnerability to production. October 5th, 12:17pm Completed a review of the logs. Confirming all identified activity was from the researcher (verified by IP Address and user agent). We resolved the vulnerability within 26 hours of its initial report, and additional security audits were completed by February 2025. Actions and remediations These are some of the actions that we have already taken : Immediate fixes Rotated all sensitive tokens. Patched the vulnerability by removing the Firebase Service Account token and implemented a restricted-access solution, granting only the minimal permissions necessary for builds. Enhanced alerts for suspicious usage of sensitive access tokens. Long-term enhancements Security audits and testing Completed a third-party security audit with independent cybersecurity company, Doyensec. The audit was completed on January 21st, 2025. A subsequent retest was completed on February 25th, 2025. We are committing to undertake annual security audits in the future. Access control and authentication All customers must now use a security key ( WebAuthn token ) to release app updates, ensuring only authorized releases. This key-based authentication is managed separately from our main systems to prevent unauthorized access even if other parts of our infrastructure are compromised. Implemented access control permissions for build and release processes, allowing account admins to assign specific permissions to team members and restrict sensitive actions. To prevent unauthorized additions to teams, inviting new users now requires authentication with a security key, ensuring only authorized admins can expand access. Sensitive actions, such as updating secrets or inviting new users, now trigger notification emails to the account owner. Infrastructure and tooling We’ve applied the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP) to our ephemeral build containers, meaning each process has only the minimum access needed to function. We’ve also open-sourced two tools we built to help achieve this: KeyVault Gatekeeper and Firestore PoLP . Introduced an option for customers to self-host updates and downloads . The source code is freely available and open-source, with setup instructions accessible on GitHub . This allows customers to manage their own self-hosted update and download infrastructure if they choose. Added security policy and security features documents to our website. How this affects you No action is required. No malicious usage was detected. The vulnerability was patched within 26 hours of first being reported. This leak occurred because the build container had broader permissions than necessary, allowing a postinstall script in an application's package.json to retrieve Firebase credentials. We have since changed our architecture so that this can not happen again, see the " Infrastructure and tooling " and " Access control and authentication " sections above for more information about our fixes. Had this vulnerability not been identified and responsibly disclosed, a malicious actor could have potentially caused significant harm. In the worst case, this would have allowed an attacker to access the ToDesktop database, user accounts, and deploy unauthorized updates to applications. I’m grateful that the security researcher came forward and disclosed the vulnerability responsibly. Why are we disclosing now? Since no malicious activity occurred, we followed industry-standard advice indicating immediate disclosure was not required. However, in the spirit of transparency, we chose to disclose after completing internal and third-party audits. Conclusion We sincerely regret that our security measures fell short, potentially putting customer applications at risk. However, I am proud of ToDesktop's rapid response in addressing the vulnerability and our proactive steps to enhance the platform's security. While the initial report and fix occurred in October 2024, we took additional time to complete a third-party audit with Doyensec, finalized on February 25th, 2025. After undertaking internal and third-party audits, we are confident in the security and resilience of the ToDesktop platform. This incident has reinforced our commitment to security, and we are dedicated to continuously improving our processes to protect our customers and their applications. We thank the security researcher, T/A xyz3va, for identifying and responsibly disclosing this vulnerability. She has shared more technical details here . No malicious usage was detected. If you have any concerns or questions, please contact us at security@todesktop.com .

title: Introducing Andromeda, our rapidly reusable high-performance upper-stage rocket engine
summary: Updated design upgrades performance, simplicity, and rapid reusability. At Stoke, we’re laser-focused on our mission to enable seamless mobility to, through, and from space by using rockets that are fully, rapidly, and reliably reusable. To achieve this,...
body_text: Updated design upgrades performance, simplicity, and rapid reusability. At Stoke, we’re laser-focused on our mission to enable seamless mobility to, through, and from space by using rockets that are fully, rapidly, and reliably reusable. To achieve this, we’re constantly learning through test and iteration. Each new design moves us closer to the holy grail of our industry: 100% full and rapid reusability. Today we’re announcing the next iteration of our upper-stage engine, which we’re naming Andromeda. Built on lessons from earlier variants, Andromeda’s new design (called Andromeda 2) brings major improvements to performance, simplicity, and rapid reusability. With Andromeda 2 now mounted on its test stand at our Moses Lake Test Site, it’s time to dive into what’s new and why it matters. Rendering of the Andromeda 2 upper stage rocket engine, including its integrated re-entry heat shield, shown here installed on Stoke’s reusable upper stage rocket. A major leap for reusability We view upper-stage reusability as the last major challenge that must be conquered before launch costs go down, and availability and reliability go up, each by an order of magnitude. It’s a problem that’s faced the industry for decades, and rapidly reusing a high-performance upper-stage rocket engine is a major part of that challenge. By integrating a metal heat shield with the engine, and by actively cooling it with liquid hydrogen, Stoke has created a system that can not only robustly survive the environments of orbital reentry, but can be ready to fly again immediately without inspection or refurbishment. It is truly the first of its kind. As with any new technology, incremental improvements bridge the gap between early prototype and mature form. While Andromeda 1 proved that the concept works through a robust test program, including a vertical takeoff and vertical landing “ Hopper ” flight, Andromeda 2 has better ascent performance, better downmass (space-to-earth transport) capacity, fewer parts, and it weighs less. It also looks a bit different. The following explains what’s involved in these changes. Andromeda 1, which combines a high-performance rocket engine with a liquid-cooled heat shield for upper-stage re-entry protection, is seen here on a flight demonstrating its vertical takeoff and vertical landing capabilities. Thruster design improvements: With Andromeda 2, we reduced the number of thrusters from 30 to 24 (but increased their individual size) and simplified the flow circuits to reduce the number of parts and to save weight without compromising thrust precision or thrust vector control. We also improved the thruster injector design, which now delivers better performance and further improves engine efficiency Andromeda 2’s thruster nozzles are now designed to operate in two different modes: one in the vacuum of space and one inside the atmosphere. The vacuum nozzle produces a high expansion ratio for improved performance in space, and the sea-level nozzle is designed to produce stable plume expansion inside the pressure of the atmosphere during propulsive landing maneuvers. Base heat shield changes: The second-stage base heat shield is one of our differentiating elements. It serves not just as armor, but as an integral part of the Andromeda engine. By applying regenerative cooling—a technology proven to work for rocket engine chambers in which the thermal environment is about 20 times more intense—Stoke has created a heat shield that can readily handle atmospheric reentry and be ready for the next flight without refurbishment. While these fundamentals remain unchanged, the new design features a different form factor. Andromeda 2’s base shape returns to one of our earliest concepts, featuring a continuously curved contour across the entire base of the vehicle, and the thruster nozzles fully embedded along the outer circumference. This geometry reduces weight compared to Andromeda 1, increases downmass capacity, and together with the new thruster nozzles, enables a more definitive qualification program in which we can test the thruster ignition and operation in vacuum conditions at our ground test facilities. This mitigates a big risk ahead of our first orbital launch. Andromeda 2 (right) seen in its shipping fixture next to Zenith (left) on Jan. 27. Increased serviceability of the engine: Packaging, access, and serviceability are difficult constraints in any aerospace design, and Andromeda’s form factor presents some unique challenges. For Andromeda 2, design efforts have focused on turbomachinery and instrumentation placement, feedline design, and thruster pod connections to better optimize operability. These changes further reduce complexity and allow the entire engine to be serviced—or even replaced—within hours or minutes. Rapid turnaround isn’t merely a goal, it’s baked into the design. Looking up at Andromeda 2 installed on Stoke’s hydrogen engine test stand. Stage 1 interface and hot staging: As we have progressed from concept demonstration to orbital vehicle design, we put concerted effort into the stage-to-stage interface. The result elegantly ties Andromeda’s heat shield to Stage 1 during ascent and effectively eliminates the need for the interstage volume (and mass) that accommodates the large bell nozzles on typical upper-stage engines. When fixed to Stage 1 during ascent, Andromeda’s thrusters are positioned outboard of the Stage 1 outer diameter. This allows Andromeda to ignite while still attached to the first stage without causing damage to the base of Stage 2, and without the need for a heavy one-time-use interstage shield to protect Stage 1. This “hot staging” operation reduces gravity losses from the flight profile, eliminates the need for stage separation pushers, and overall significantly improves Nova’s mass capacity to orbit. Numerical simulation of hot staging maneuver, showing Andromeda’s plume flowing outboard of Nova’s Stage 1 structure. Why all of this matters Stoke was founded with the goal of making the space economy a natural extension of the global economy. That will require seamless mobility to, through, and from space, which we believe is only possible with reliable and rapidly reusable transportation services. It’s not just rocket science, it’s common sense; efficient and durable designs that reduce complexity lead to better performance and faster turnarounds. With Andromeda 2, we are one step closer to that vision. The changes we’ve made to evolve Andromeda 1 aren’t just about improving performance, they’re about making our Nova rocket practical for everyday use. We’re excited about what that represents not only for Stoke, but for the future of space development: lower costs, better availability, higher reliability, and access to any orbit at any time. The era of full and rapid reuse is just around the corner! Ad astra per aspera. title: Expanding Access to Radiotherapy in Ghana: A Conversation with Rev. Dr. Kofi Adesi Kyei
summary: Closing care gaps is a big challenge. Learn from Dr Kyei on how expanding access to radiotherapy is critical for patients in Ghana.
body_text: Among the well-reported disparities in access to cancer treatment across Africa, the radiotherapy care gaps are perhaps most evident. GLOBOCAN data estimated that current radiotherapy capacity meets only 30 percent of the need across Africa.1 Ghana is recognized as a leader in improving the availability of radiotherapy — both within the country and across the continent. Despite this, persistent gaps in access to radiotherapy within Ghana signal much work left to be done: Research from 2020 estimated that just 23 percent of patients requiring external beam radiotherapy actually receive that critical treatment.2 We had a conversation with Rev. Dr. Kofi Adesi Kyei, (Chief Radiation Therapist at the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital) who heads the Department of Radiography and Radiation Therapy at the University of Ghana, about the multifactorial nature of the barriers to radiotherapy in Ghana. Dr. Kyei shared how he and his peers are pushing a three-pronged effort — among the public, within government health agencies, and within the broader clinical oncology community across Africa — to raise awareness of the importance of radiotherapy as part of holistic cancer care. Limited radiotherapy equipment creates geographic barriers and long wait times A 2021 whitepaper found that the average density of radiotherapy units in high-resource countries is 7.24 per million people.3 In contrast, Ghana had an estimated population of 31.1 million in 2022 with only 5 external beam radiotherapy treatment machines (EBRT), that equates to 1 per 6.22 million (0.17 EBRT units per million population).4 Moreover, these radiotherapy units are located at only three centers — two public and one private. Three machines in the Greater Accra region, where Dr. Kyei practices, serve a population of 12 to 14 million, while the single linac and one cobalt in the Ashanti region of Ghana covers roughly the same population — in addition to a large number of non-Ghanaians coming across the border to receive radiotherapy treatments. This makes geography one of the biggest barriers to accessing radiotherapy, creating significant care gaps even within Ghana. In the 2021 study, 30 percent of eligible patients in the Greater Accra region received radiotherapy treatment, compared to just 1 percent of eligible patients in the country’s more rural northern region.5 Dr. Kyei said that this also puts a heavy burden on Ghana’s three radiotherapy centers. “The number of patients is shooting up,” he said, noting that the cancer incidence globally is predicted to double by 2040.5 “Currently, we treat about 100 patients a day at each of the public centers,” he said. “Our clinics are always busy; the whole place is packed with patients.” “The high demand in the public treatment centers means patients typically wait three weeks — and as much as six weeks — to receive treatment. Wait times are much shorter at the private treatment center — generally just a few days — but most patients cannot afford the cost of care at the private center,” says Dr Kyei. Dr. Kyei says Ghana is working on obtaining additional radiotherapy units. “If we get equipment, that would be a very huge burden lifted for us,” he says. But Ghana is also exploring innovative treatment modalities, like hypofractionation and hyper-fractionation, to increase the volume of patients that the public centers can treat. “We are trying to enroll more patients into hypofractionation treatments, because we want to be able to treat more patients, as quickly as possible,” Dr. Kyei explains. Changing cultural perceptions of cancer: Key to addressing late presentation burden Dr Kyei reports that “breast cancer is the most common indication treated at the public treatment centers in Ghana, followed by pelvic cancers (cervical and prostate), and head and neck cancers.” One common challenge across all indications is that most patients arrive for treatment at later stages of disease. “Late presentation is quite a huge burden for us,” says Dr. Kyei. “We need to do more to raise awareness in the population.” Adding to this challenge, these patient-awareness campaigns are largely dependent on the same clinicians who are already stretched thin trying to meet demand for treatment. Dr. Kyei highlights three main barriers that prevent patients from coming in earlier for treatment. Long distance travel and cost are the two well-known challenges with clearer (albeit difficult to achieve) solutions. But the third barrier — cultural perceptions of cancer and superstitions around medical treatment — is a much more nuanced issue to tackle. “Patients often start with alternative cures or treatments before they come to us,” says Dr. Kyei. Some are afraid to visit a hospital for a screening. “They would prefer any other place than coming to the hospital,” he says. Other patients directly challenge their cancer diagnosis. “Some will not even want to hear the word cancer — they say, ‘No, don’t say that I have cancer,’” Dr. Kyei explains. Nevertheless, Dr. Kyei notes that it wasn’t that long ago that similar attitudes prevailed in more developed countries. He advocates a more empathetic, education-based approach: “You need to meet them where they’re at,” he says. “When we get them in and show them numbers and educate them on outcomes, we help change those perceptions.” Yet, here again, the limited time of Ghana’s clinical oncology community presents challenges. “You need time to talk to patients — to explain things to them,” Dr. Kyei says. “And we are few, so we have to work within the capacity we have.” Despite government assistance, cost remains a huge barrier The Ghanaian government has taken significant steps to address the cost barriers to healthcare, including government assistance programs tailored for cancer treatment. “The government is trying to help,” says Dr. Kyei, “But to be frank, they don’t fund some of the things we need.” Some kinds of cancer care, such as breast cancer surgeries, are fully covered by government assistance. But radiotherapy is not covered, nor are radiological and pathological services that cancer patients typically require. “All the imaging and exams — patients have to pay out of pocket,” explains Dr. Kyei. “It’s a much lower cost than the private center. But in the eyes of a Ghanaian, it’s still a big barrier.” The two treatment centers run by the University of Ghana have developed some creative approaches to easing this cost burden for patients, while still delivering a high quality of care. Dr. Kyei says his centers use a CT simulator to plan treatments, but also have a conventional simulator they use for 2D cases — primarily for palliative patients. “But if a patient is not able to afford CT simulation, we still do the 2D for them,” he explains. “We call it 2.5 — we do the 2D and try to take contours and images, and then we send it to planning to see if we can add in some wedges.” Raising government awareness of the need for holistically covered cancer care Dr. Kyei says there are many instances where government coverage limitations lead to substandard treatment. “If you are doing a mastectomy, but then you cannot pay for radiotherapy or chemotherapy, you’re kind of back to square one,” he says. “We all know the recurrence statistics. So, if the patient has surgery but cannot afford radiotherapy or chemotherapy, they go home and in three months, the whole thing has metastasized.” Similar situations exist in other countries in Africa. “I was in Kenya recently,” says Dr. Kyei, “and the insurance is there, but it doesn’t cover everything, especially for cancer care.” While Dr. Kyei stresses that some assistance is better than none, one of his main focuses is advocating for a more holistic coverage of cancer treatment. “We need to increase government understanding,” he says. “We need to talk directly to the government and say, ‘If you want to help the patients entirely, you need to provide holistic treatment.’” Not only would this holistic coverage help to improve outcomes for patients that receive treatment, but it would also help to bring more eligible patients in earlier. “Because if I know I cannot afford the treatment, I will not even go,” says Dr. Kyei. Sharing resources and insights across Africa As part of his public awareness and policy advocacy work, Dr. Kyei is heavily involved in the Global Coalition of Radiotherapy and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). Much of his recent work has focused on addressing regional disparities across Africa. He notes that the northern and southern regions of Africa are much more advanced, while the eastern and western regions still face significant challenges. “Our focus is to see how we can bridge the gap,” he says. “I go around seeing how I can bring resources to other countries to help level the grounds for cancer care.” Dr. Kyei has brought this same message into his work educating the next generation of clinicians in Africa. “When I bring students from other parts of Africa to Ghana, we train them not only on how to do the clinical work, but also to see what can be done to improve cancer care in their home countries,” he says. While a lot of clinical students end up leaving their home countries, Dr. Kyei says he tells them, “Wherever you find yourself, see how you can give back to Africa: online sessions, meeting students or colleagues, sharing your experiences and insights — whatever you can do.” Progress may look slow, but the impact on patients is huge Assessing the impact that he and his peers have had in improving radiotherapy in Ghana and across Africa, Dr. Kyei says the progress is clear to see. “In Ghana, we used to have patients coming from many countries that did not have radiotherapy at all,” he says. “But now, some of these countries have one or two machines.” Expanding access to radiotherapy in other African nations directly reduces the burden on Ghana’s radiotherapy treatment centers, helping to reduce wait times and bring critical treatment to more Ghanaians. He notes that closing care gaps is undoubtedly a big challenge and a slow process, “But you need to start somewhere, and I’m sure we’re going to get there.” Perhaps most importantly, while that progress may look slow from a wider perspective, bringing better treatment to more patients has a profound impact on those individuals. That’s what makes it all worth it for Dr. Kyei. “Whatever we can do to help our patients,” he says. “When they are happy and they appreciate what we are doing, it is so satisfying — beyond everything else.” Read more stories about gaps in care across the globe References Elmore SNC, et al. Stability programs are systematic testing protocols designed to evaluate how a supplement’s quality and safety are affected by environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, and light exposure over time. These programs aim to determine the product’s shelf life and establish proper storage and handling guidelines, ensuring that supplements remain effective and safe for consumers throughout their lifecycle. Importance for Consumer Safety Without proper stability testing, supplements can degrade, losing their effectiveness or even posing safety risks. Stability programs ensure the product delivers on its intended benefits, fostering consumer confidence. With NAI’s expertise, supplements undergo rigorous stability testing to validate their durability and performance, giving manufacturers and consumers peace of mind. Meeting Regulatory Standards Regulatory bodies, including the FDA, mandate stability testing for dietary supplements to ensure compliance with safety and labeling standards. NAI helps brands navigate these regulations, providing stability programs that align with industry requirements and support smooth product launches. Stability Programs How Stability Testing Protects Dietary Supplement Potency and Consumer Trust Preserving Potency Active ingredients in supplements, such as vitamins, minerals, and patented compounds like CarnoSyn ® Beta-Alanine , can degrade over time, reducing their effectiveness. Stability testing evaluates how well these ingredients retain their potency throughout the product’s shelf life. Specialized formulations, such as TriBsyn™ and SR CarnoSyn ® , require tailored stability programs to ensure their unique benefits remain intact. Maintaining Physical Integrity In addition to ingredient potency, stability testing assesses the product’s physical properties, such as tablet hardness, capsule integrity, and powder flowability. These factors influence consumer experience and satisfaction, making stability testing a critical step in production. Building Consumer Trust Transparent stability data reassures consumers that the product will perform as promised. Accurate expiration dates and storage instructions enhance brand credibility and foster long-term trust. By leveraging NAI’s testing services, brands can confidently communicate their product’s reliability and safety. Stability programs identify potential issues before the product reaches the market, reducing risks and ensuring cost-effective production. NAI’s proactive approach helps brands avoid financial losses and maintain a positive market presence. Key Factors in Designing an Effective Stability Program for Dietary Supplements Tailoring Programs to Specific Products Each supplement requires a unique stability program based on its formulation, packaging , and intended storage conditions. For instance, moisture-sensitive powders need testing under controlled humidity levels. NAI customizes stability programs to meet the specific needs of each product, ensuring precise and reliable results. Simulating Real-World Conditions Stability testing simulates environmental conditions the product may encounter during transportation, storage, and consumer use. By testing at varying temperatures and humidity levels, NAI helps brands establish optimal storage guidelines and accurate shelf life estimates. Adhering to Regulatory Guidelines An effective stability program complies with global regulatory standards, including FDA requirements, proper certifications , and current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP). NAI’s experienced team ensures all testing aligns with these regulations, streamlining the approval process for new products and maintaining compliance for existing ones. Regular Monitoring and Reevaluation Stability testing is not a one-time process. Regular monitoring ensures that products continue to meet quality standards throughout their lifespan. title: Our Upholstery, Our Legacy
summary: Arhaus’ legacy with handcrafted upholstery began not long after we opened our doors in 1986. Our business was growing, as was the need to offer exceptional upholstered seating to our customers. And I knew exactly what I wanted our assortment to be. Silhouettes and fabrics that felt current but timeless. Frames made from sustainably sourced wood. Heirloom quality that would last. When I couldn’t find what I wanted, I set out to build it myself. I drove through the foothills of North Carolina, the epicenter of American upholstery making, and met with workshops of all sizes. Eventually, I found artisans who shared my vision—many of whom we still work with today. Cutters of fabric and leather. Tailors. Frame builders. Each one working with a masterful precision matched only by their passion for quality. From that initial journey almost forty years ago, Arhaus Upholstery has grown to include more than 175 collections, hundreds of silhouettes, and the most exquisite materials sourced around the world. It’s so much more than that, too. It’s the sectional that hosts your family movie nights, and the recliner you sink into after a long day. The new swivel chair that updates the entire room, and the sleeper sofa you turn to whenever guests come to town. Making these pieces for you is the greatest honor in our business. In 2024, we sent a team of writers and photographers to those North Carolina foothills, where they visited our upholstery artisans. They learned about the process of furniture building—the cutting and sewing, the tufting and hand-tying—but more importantly, they learned about the people behind these practices. The hundreds of hands that touch every sofa and sectional. The laughter you can hear amid the whir of sewing machines and the clang of hammers. The importance of building things to last… and with love. I am so proud to bring our Storied series home, and to share Volume III with you. With endless gratitude, John Reed, Arhaus Co-Founder

title: AmpUp & Tritium Upgrade EV Fast Chargers
summary: AmpUp and Tritium partner to upgrade RT50 fast chargers, expanding EV charging access with enhanced performance and seamless integration.
body_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA — AmpUp, a leading provider of electric vehicle (EV) charging solutions, has announced a collaboration with Tritium, a global leader in DC fast chargers, to offer an efficient upgrade program for fast-charging stations across North America. This partnership simplifies the process for Tritium RT50 owners to integrate their charging stations into the AmpUp network, offering enhanced features to improve EV charging infrastructure and customer experiences. Seamless Integration of Tritium RT50 Chargers into AmpUp Network The program will be delivered in two phases to help Tritium RT50 owners transition smoothly to the AmpUp charging network: Phase One : This phase ensures a hassle-free integration of existing Tritium stations into the AmpUp network, enabling site hosts to provide their Tritium charger’s serial number and written approval for transfer. AmpUp will facilitate the entire integration process free of charge, offering site hosts the option to choose preferred cloud services. Phase Two : In this phase, Tritium RT50 owners have the opportunity to upgrade their chargers to a brand-new 50kW DC fast charger with several advanced features, such as dual charging capabilities, universal compatibility, and scalable power. These chargers can be easily installed on existing RT50 pads, minimizing downtime and providing a more reliable charging experience. Enhancing EV Charging Capabilities for the Future By upgrading to a new 50kW DC fast charger, Tritium RT50 owners will benefit from enhanced charging capabilities, including: Dual Charging : Charge two vehicles simultaneously, doubling charging capacity. Universal Compatibility : Support for CCS and NACS cords, enabling compatibility with virtually any electric vehicle on the market. Scalable Power : Upgradable to 75kW, providing future-proofed performance as EV demand increases. Sustainability : AmpUp ensures the responsible recycling of the old RT50 chargers, minimizing environmental impact. “This upgrade program underscores AmpUp’s commitment to advancing EV infrastructure and streamlining the transition to cleaner, more sustainable transportation,” said Tom Sun , CEO and co-founder of AmpUp. “Our collaboration with Tritium allows site hosts to modernize their charging stations with minimal disruption while unlocking the full potential of their infrastructure. Trusted by companies across industries, AmpUp’s platform helps businesses and property owners optimize the performance of their charging networks. With over 1,500 charging stations deployed in over 75 North American markets, AmpUp is at the forefront of EV charging technology. About Tritium Tritium is a global leader in the development and manufacturing of DC fast chargers for electric vehicles. Founded in 2001, Tritium designs innovative, reliable, and user-friendly chargers that support the transition to clean energy. Tritium’s compact and robust chargers are designed to thrive in harsh conditions while ensuring maximum uptime and efficiency for charging networks.

title: Coffee and Cortisol: A One-Sided Relationship
summary: Caffeine elevates your stress hormones, including cortisol. Px coffee is a practical way to supporting cortisol management... without having to give up coffee. More
body_text: Caffeine’s Relationship to Cortisol and How You Can Reduce Cortisol Levels With Coffee For many of us, coffee is more than just our favorite drink, it’s a ritual, a lifeline, and the non-negotiable start to our day. That first sip is often what pulls us out of bed and fuels our mornings. But while coffee is celebrated for its ability to wake us up and sharpen our focus, it also has a hidden side effect: it spikes our adrenaline and cortisol levels, our body’s primary stress hormones. Over time, these repeated surges in adrenaline and cortisol can leave us feeling more stressed, fatigued, and burned out—ironically, the very things we’re trying to avoid. In this post, we’ll explore the relationship between caffeine and cortisol, uncover how your morning coffee might be affecting your stress levels, and share practical tips to help you enjoy your coffee while keeping cortisol in check. And don’t worry, we’d never recommend you quit coffee. We’re here to help you enjoy coffee more, not give it up What Is Cortisol and why do your cortisol levels matter? Cortisol is most commonly recognized as the body’s “stress hormone,” but it helps orchestrate everything from your metabolism to your immune response. Produced by your adrenal glands, cortisol plays a key role in regulating your metabolism, immune system, and energy levels throughout the day. Think of it as your body’s built-in alarm system: it helps you wake up in the morning, powers you through stressful situations, and even gives you a boost to tackle midday dips in energy. Cortisol follows a natural daily rhythm, known as the circadian rhythm. It typically peaks in the early morning (around 6–9 a.m.), helping you wake up and face the day, then gradually declines throughout the day, reaching its lowest point at night as your body and mind prepare for rest and recovery ( Fries, 2008 ). However, when stress—whether physical, emotional, or environmental—triggers a cortisol release, it can throw this balance out of whack. While short-term cortisol spikes are an essential part of your body’s alarm system (i.e., helping you respond to emergencies), chronic high cortisol levels can lead to symptoms like weight gain (especially around the midsection, or ‘belly fat’), mood swings, and a weakened immune system. In short, cortisol is a double-edged sword: it’s essential for survival in small doses, but can wear us down and make us feel fatigued and burned out when levels remain chronically elevated or when our cortisol levels are repeatedly spiking. When cortisol remains elevated for too long, it can leave you feeling drained, foggy, and emotionally exhausted—common symptoms of burnout. If you're experiencing persistent fatigue and mental exhaustion, you may want to read up on how caffeine can contribute to burnout . How coffee and caffeine can elevate cortisol Within the first 30-45 minutes after waking, your cortisol levels naturally increase sharply ( Clow, 2010 ), typically reaching their highest levels early in the morning — typically between 6 a.m. and 9 a.m. This surge, often called the “cortisol awakening response,” is designed to help you wake up and feel alert. Unfortunately, this happens to be the exact time most of us reach for that first (or second and third) cup of coffee. Caffeine’s relationship with cortisol is complex—it’s not just about waking you up; it directly affects how your body responds to stress. Here’s how caffeine interacts with your stress hormones and how your coffee habit can be affecting your cortisol levels. 1. Caffeine Blocks Adenosine, Your Brain’s “Sleep Signal” Caffeine’s primary job is to block adenosine, the brain chemical that promotes relaxation and drowsiness. By doing this, you feel more alert and focused. However, this same blockade signals your body to produce adrenaline and cortisol — both of which are tied to the body’s “fight or flight” response. In other words, caffeine isn’t just telling you to wake up; it can make your body scream, “danger!”. Essentially, caffeine is hijacking a system evolved over thousands of years to help us survive life-or-death situations, like outrunning a predator on the savannah. But instead of fleeing from lions, we’re now sitting at desks, staring at laptops, and stressing over deadlines—proof that our biological wiring isn’t always the best fit for our modern lives. 2. Caffeine Can Spike Cortisol Levels Numerous studies indicate that caffeine consumption can lead to a cortisol spike, even in daily coffee drinkers ( Cole, 2024 ; Lovallo, 2005 ; Lovallo, 2006 ). While regular coffee drinkers may develop some tolerance over time, factors like stress, lack of sleep, and dehydration can amplify the effect. For example, if you exceed your usual amount of caffeine on a particularly hectic day, you might experience an even bigger surge in cortisol—and the accompanying jitters, anxiety, and wired feeling. This is why that extra cup of coffee during a stressful workweek might leave you feeling more frazzled and less focused while a cup of coffee on a calm weekend morning has no negative effects. 3. The Domino Effect on Blood Sugar and Energy Caffeine doesn’t just affect cortisol and perceived stress levels—it can also lead to a short-term spike in blood sugar by decreasing insulin sensitivity ( Shi, 2016 ; van Dam, 2004 ). In simpler terms, caffeine makes it harder for your body to process sugar efficiently, which can contribute to the energy crash you may feel later in the day. If you’ve ever experienced a “coffee crash” a few hours after drinking coffee, this cortisol-blood sugar connection might be to blame. It’s a double whammy: caffeine gives you a quick boost, but the resulting cortisol spike and blood sugar imbalance can leave you feeling even more drained than before. Now that we’ve explored how caffeine affects cortisol, let’s look at why timing matters—especially first thing in the morning—and how a few strategic tweaks to your routine can help you maintain steady energy levels all day long. Signs of High Cortisol & Adrenaline From Too Much Caffeine Caffeine's dark side: spikes in stress hormones Short-term spikes in adrenaline and cortisol, like the kind you may experience after drinking too much coffee, typically show up in a combination of physical and mental/emotional symptoms. Common physical signs of high adrenaline and high cortisol levels Increased Heart Rate & Blood Pressure – The initial surge of adrenaline (with some contribution from cortisol) triggers your body’s fight-or-flight response, making your heart beat faster. Sweating or Feeling Hot – Adrenaline revs up energy production, releasing energy quickly and causing mild sweating or flushing. Jitters, Tremors, or Muscle Twitches – Elevated cortisol can exacerbate adrenaline’s effects on our nervous system leading to tremors or twitching. Tension Headaches – Muscle tightness in the shoulders and neck can lead to headaches. Common mental signs of high adrenaline and high cortisol levels Racing Thoughts / Overthinking – Heightened adrenaline and cortisol can make your mind feel like it’s on overdrive, leaving you feeling “wired.” Irritability or Mood Swings – Sudden spikes in stress hormones may lead to feeling on edge and moodiness. Anxiety or Feeling ‘On High Alert’ – A surge of both cortisol and adrenaline can trigger physical and emotional stress responses that resemble an anxiety attack, even when there’s no actual threat. Brain Fog or Difficulty Focusing – In small doses, adrenaline and cortisol can boost alertness. However, when these hormones remain high for too long (e.g., from excessive caffeine), you might experience scattered thoughts, difficulty concentrating, and a mental haze commonly referred to as brain fog. Put simply, caffeine blocks adenosine receptors in the brain, which normally help calm the nervous system. In response, your body steps on the gas — releasing adrenaline and cortisol. Adrenaline is released first and fastest, contributing to the immediate “jittery” sensations; cortisol increases contribute to longer-lasting feelings of stress or anxiety. Thus, if you’ve ever described yourself as “over-caffeinated,” you were likely experiencing a spike in both adrenaline and cortisol. These effects are common, but they are also signs that your body is mounting a stress response. How to Reduce Cortisol Levels Without Giving Up Coffee Px Coffee: A New Way to Help Manage Cortisol Spikes Px, or paraxanthine, is a metabolite of caffeine—meaning your body naturally converts some of the caffeine you consume into paraxanthine. Like caffeine, Px increases alertness, but early research points to Px having fewer stress-related side effects -- like sharp adrenaline spikes and increased cortisol levels. This makes it a gentler option for people who are looking for a morning (or mid-afternoon) coffee without caffeine's harsh effects on the nervous system. Px coffee delivers energy and alertness, but without hijacking your body's stress response. How Px Works Less Adrenaline Jolt : Some preliminary findings ( e.g. , Benowitz, 1995 ) indicate that paraxanthine might have a milder impact on the sympathetic nervous system, which could lead to less of a “fight-or-flight” response than regular caffeine—especially at lower doses. Sustained Energy Without the Jitters: Because paraxanthine is absorbed, crosses the blood-brain barrier, and is metabolized at different rates than caffeine ( Birkett, 1986 ), there is evidence it offers a smoother energy boost without the abrupt highs and lows ( Benowitz, 1995 ). If you’re prone to caffeine-induced stress or jitteriness, or if you’re looking to keep your stress hormones in better balance, Px Coffee could be a great option. It supports a more controlled response to caffeine, helping to minimize cortisol spikes while still providing a boost of energy. Smooth, sustained energy to help you both wake up and power through the day A kinder caffeine that doesn't overstimulate your nervous system Better focus, fewer jitters letting you actually focus on getting your work done Less impact on sleep quality because Px doesn’t linger in your body like caffeine Final Thoughts: There are Simple Solutions to Help Manage Cortisol Coffee can be part of a balanced lifestyle, but it’s crucial to understand how it interacts with stress hormones, including cortisol. Small adjustments—like timing your morning cup, pairing coffee with food, and prioritizing sleep—can make a big difference in helping you feel your best. For those particularly sensitive to caffeine’s effects, Px coffee offers a gentler alternative that may help you avoid cortisol spikes and energy crashes.By pairing your coffee habit with smart choices, you can stay energized, focused, and stress-free—without giving up your favorite brew. Ready to take control of your cortisol levels? Start by trying one of these tips today and see how your body responds.

title: Stripe Guide: manage Stripe billing lifecycle and reporting
summary: As we partnered with Stripe, we've been digging into subscription data with our tools and have spotted some interesting patterns - for example: sometimes the way subscription statuses look isn't exactly how they're acting. These are the kind of things that can easily fly under the radar, and we want to help you catch them. Please add yours in the comment
body_text: The Fundamental Challenge in Subscription Status Management Current Industry Standard: A Simplistic Approach Many teams rely on Stripe Billing features like Subscriptions and Entitlements to provision customer access to product features. As suggested by Stripe for ease of integration, customers often use the subscription status (IF status=active ) as the sole determinant for granting or revoking access to paid features. While this approach seems intuitive, it masks several complex underlying issues that can dramatically impact revenue integrity and customer entitlements. Deep Dive: Limitations in Subscription Status Determination Stripe's method of determining subscription status primarily based on the latest invoice status introduces several challenges, as will be detailed in the following sections. 1. Uncollectible Invoices and Active Subscriptions Anomaly: Issue: Even if the latest subscription invoice is marked as 'uncollectible' (e.g., due to failed payment), the subscription status remains 'active' in Stripe. Impact: This can falsely indicate an active subscription, granting users continued access to paid features despite non-payment, leading to revenue leakage. Recommended Actions: Stripe's Revenue Recovery : When utilizing Stripe's smart retries, ensure to explicitly configure the invoice and connected subscription statuses for unsuccessful recoveries through the Stripe UI. This facilitates proper management of subscription statuses following the recovery process. Stripe's configurable automation is limited and doesn’t support advanced status configurations, potentially restricting flexibility for complex billing scenarios. Custom Billing Automations : For payment recovery or internal billing operations requiring specific statuses beyond Stripe's limited automation UI, leveraging the Stripe API provides granular control over subscription lifecycle management, though this approach demands dedicated development resources to implement and maintain effectively. Asynchronous Payments Masking Subscription Payment Failures: Issue: When a recurring subscription invoice is 'open' and the customer modifies their subscription, Stripe creates a separate proration invoice ( proration_behavior=always_invoice ). If this proration invoice is immediately paid or has a $0 amount, Stripe will show the subscription as 'active' due to this being the latest successful payment, even if the original recurring invoice remains unpaid. Similarly, successful one-time payments related to the subscription (e.g., add-ons or extra usage) can also cause the subscription to appear 'active' despite an unpaid recurring invoice, potentially leading to inaccurate access management. Impact: This can mislead into believing the subscription is still valid, again leading to inappropriate access control. Recommended Actions: When a subscription is 'past-due' , restrict customers from making changes to their subscription plan that could trigger Stripe's proration flow. This prevents the creation of one-time invoices (with billing_reason=subscription_update ) under the subscription that are separate from the original billing cycle invoices (with billing_reason=subscription_cycle ). Consider disabling the billing update section in your app for past-due accounts, prompting customers to settle outstanding invoices before making changes or to contact support. Additionally, if possible, generate invoices for one-time purchases separately from the recurring subscription to maintain clearer billing distinctions. Refund Invoice Misrepresentation Issue : Stripe marks refund invoices as 'paid' , which doesn’t represent the actual subscription status when this is the latest invoice. Impact: Introduces potential synchronization challenges between billing and the product entitlement systems. Recommended Actions: When processing refunds, proactively verify the subscription status before creating the refund invoice, and if the status has been altered, revert it to the previous state. Additionally, consider implementing an internal operational policy that allows discretion in withholding refunds for delinquent customers. Recommended Subscriptions lifecycle To mitigate these challenges, we recommend developing a multi-layered approach to subscription status management: 1. Define Your Own Cancellation Logic Create a custom cancellation flows that take into account more nuanced factors beyond Stripe’s latest subscription’s invoice logic and the basic post recovery status automation. This ensures that access to services based on the subscription status (Entitlement) is managed more accurately and in line with actual payment statuses. 2. Do Not Rely Solely on Stripe's Subscription Status Enhance your status verification by implementing custom validation logic beyond Stripe's default status, that can be achieved by: Carefully processing all Stripe webhooks events Cross-referencing multiple invoice and payment signals Creating a more nuanced entitlement determination process 3. Run a Proactive Anomaly Detection with FlyCode Run real-time monitoring for payment and subscription inconsistencies Create alert mechanisms for unusual billing patterns Develop flexible response mechanisms for various billing scenarios Establish automated remediation workflows Maintain clear documentation of edge cases and resolutions There are many more nuances to this as there are with each of your businesses so it’s important to adjust the settings and reporting to you. If you want help with this, please reach out and we’d love to help you for free. You can reach out here or to install our Stripe app .
